title: Identifying severe COVID-19 risk variants modulating enhancer reporter activity in lung cells.
authors: Weykopf, Giovanna; Bickmore, Wendy A; Biddie, Simon C; Friman, Elias T
one_liner_zh: 该文通过大规模报告基因实验和深度学习模型识别影响肺细胞调控活性的新冠重症风险变异，虽涉及转录因子候选，但核心是变异调控功能注释而非TF-DNA互作建模，方法可迁移性有限。
abstract: Common genetic variants contribute to risk for complex human diseases. However, despite thousands of associations, variants modulating disease risk and their functional impact remain largely unknown. This includes SARS-CoV-2 infection, where outcomes range from asymptomatic to fatal. Most genetic risk variants associated with COVID-19 disease, identified through genome wide association studies, are located in the non-coding genome and may function by altering gene expression in disease-relevant cells and tissues. To address this at scale, we tested >4800 severe COVID-19-associated variants to determine the impact of individual variants and variant combinations on regulatory activity using Self-Transcribing Active Regulatory Region sequencing, a massively-parallel reporter assay. Focusing on variants that may have their impact in the lung, in a lung epithelial cell line (A549) we identify 166 variants within active sequences, of which 29 modulate activity allele-specifically. Evaluating variant combinations, we observe both additive and non-additive effects on regulatory activity. We employ state-of-the-art deep learning models to interpret allele-specific variant effects on regulatory activity and endogenous genomic features. Our work provides a set of prioritised severe COVID-19-associated variants that modulate regulatory activity in lung epithelial cells, candidate transcription factors, and candidate target genes with potential to be disease modifying.
abstract_zh: 常见遗传变异会增加复杂人类疾病的患病风险。然而，尽管已发现数千种关联，但调节疾病风险的变异及其功能影响在很大程度上仍属未知。这包括SARS-CoV-2感染，其结局范围从无症状到致命不等。通过全基因组关联研究识别出的与COVID-19疾病相关的大多数遗传风险变异位于非编码基因组中，可能通过改变疾病相关细胞和组织中的基因表达来发挥作用。为大规模解决这一问题，我们测试了超过4800个与重症COVID-19相关的变异，利用自我转录活性调控区测序（一种大规模平行报告基因检测）来确定单个变异及变异组合对调控活性的影响。聚焦于可能在肺部产生影响的变异，在肺上皮细胞系（A549）中，我们识别出166个位于活性序列内的变异，其中29个以等位基因特异性方式调节活性。在评估变异组合时，我们观察到对调控活性的加性效应和非加性效应。我们采用最先进的深度学习模型来解读等位基因特异性变异对调控活性和内源基因组特征的影响。我们的工作提供了一组优先化的重症COVID-19相关变异，这些变异在肺上皮细胞中调节调控活性，并确定了候选转录因子和候选靶基因，它们具有改变疾病进程的潜力。
